ai.description: This 15 cm skink has a brown body with dark-spotted sides and a pale venter. It features a wedge-shaped snout, reduced limbs, and a long, cylindrical tail. It belongs to the family Scincidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Madras Spotted Skink is best identified by its extremely elongated, snake-like body and vestigial limbs, which are significantly smaller than those of other Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: The Madras Spotted Skink inhabits leaf litter and loose soil within tropical deciduous forests and coastal scrublands, typically at low elevations near the Indian coast.
ai.behavior: The Madras Spotted Skink is a fossorial lizard that spends much of its time burrowing beneath leaf litter and loose soil to remain concealed from predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Barkudia insularis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Barkudia insularis is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily found in the coastal plains of Odisha, particularly near Chilika Lake, at low elevations.
